status_summary: Section 50203 of Public Law 119-21 directed Interior to make at least 4 million additional acres available for coal leasing, and BLM's notice of 2025-10-02 made about 13.1 million acres available without itself issuing leases. The first two sales did not produce a lease: the only bid at the Spring Creek (Montana) sale held 2025-10-06, about 186,000 dollars from Navajo Transitional Energy Company, was later rejected by Interior as not meeting Mineral Leasing Act requirements, and the West Antelope III (Wyoming) sale set for 2025-10-08 was postponed with no new date (both per news reports), and a Federal Register search of BLM coal documents from 2025-10-15 through 2026-10-07 found no further Wyoming or Montana sale or lease-by-application notice. On 2025-12-11 the President approved Congressional Review Act resolutions disapproving the 2024 Buffalo (Wyoming) plan amendment (Public Law 119-51) and the 2024 Miles City (Montana) plan amendment (Public Law 119-48), which removed those amendments' coal limits and restored the earlier plans. On 2026-06-04 BLM ended the separate amendment processes it had begun in July 2025 for both offices, reporting 2,614,310 (Buffalo) and 6,989,390 (Miles City) coal acres available for further consideration for leasing.

timeline.event: Public Law 119-21 is enacted (GovInfo dates it 2025-07-04); its section 50203 concerns leases for known recoverable coal resources. BLM's 2025-10-02 notice (below) describes it as requiring Interior to make at least 4 million additional acres of federal mineral estate with known recoverable coal available for leasing within 90 days.

BLM publishes a direct final rule (90 FR 36122, effective 2025-09-30 unless significant adverse comments were received) revising its coal royalty regulations at 43 CFR part 3470 to carry out changes required by Public Law 119-21; the rate changes themselves were not read.

BLM notices a sealed-bid competitive sale of federal coal at the Spring Creek Mine, Big Horn County, Montana, with bids due 2025-10-06. Interior's release of 2025-09-02 announced the sale for 2025-10-06 (sealed bids due 2025-10-03), covering about 1,262 acres and an estimated 167.5 million tons of recoverable coal.
BLM notices a sealed-bid competitive sale of the West Antelope III lease-by-application, Campbell County, Wyoming, with sale on 2025-10-08.
BLM publishes its notice making about 13.1 million acres available for coal leasing under section 50203; future applications remain subject to existing leasing requirements.

The Spring Creek, Montana coal lease sale draws a single sealed bid, about $186,000 from Navajo Transitional Energy Company for a 1,262-acre tract; Interior later rejects it as not meeting Mineral Leasing Act requirements (reported by E&E News on 2025-10-10; WyoFile reported on 2025-10-08 that the bid was still under review).
The West Antelope III (Wyoming) coal lease sale, scheduled for this date, is postponed with no new date set (per WyoFile, published 2025-10-08).

The President approves Public Law 119-51 (H.J. Res. 130), a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving the Bureau of Land Management's Buffalo Field Office record of decision and approved resource management plan amendment, providing that it has no force or effect; BLM's 2026-06-04 notice describes the effect as restoring the earlier Buffalo plan.

The President approves Public Law 119-48 (H.J. Res. 104), a Congressional Review Act resolution disapproving BLM's Miles City Field Office record of decision and approved resource management plan amendment of 2024-11-20, providing that it has no force or effect.

BLM ends the Buffalo (Wyoming, doc 2026-11151) and Miles City (Montana, doc 2026-11149) plan amendment processes begun by notices of intent of 2025-07-08; the notices treat the 2024 amendments disapproved by Congress as never in effect and report 2,614,310 (Buffalo) and 6,989,390 (Miles City) BLM coal acres available for further consideration for leasing.

title: Restart federal coal leasing in Wyoming and Montana
uncertainties: The Federal Register search used the term coal for BLM documents only; a sale noticed under a different title or by another office could have been missed, and no news search covered 2026 sale developments beyond one query. No BLM or Interior release announcing the rejection of the Spring Creek bid or the postponement of West Antelope III was found (a search returned only a 2011 BLM release on a different sale), so those two outcomes still rest on E&E News and WyoFile. Interior's release of 2025-09-02 gives sealed-bid receipt on 2025-10-03 and the sale on 2025-10-06, while the Federal Register notice of 2025-09-15 as summarized earlier gave bids due 2025-10-06; the sale day of 2025-10-06 is used. The 2025-08-01 BLM coal royalty rule was read only through its summary page and its rate changes were not reviewed. Public Law 119-51 is now confirmed by govinfo (H.J. Res. 130, approved 2025-12-11). Secretarial Order 3348's reinstatement was not verified. Freshness pass of 2026-10-16: the Federal Register API was searched for BLM coal documents published from 2026-06-05 (five results, none a Wyoming or Montana sale or lease notice) and for coal lease documents from any agency since 2025-10-15 (four results; the only lease-by-application item is in West Virginia); the BLM Wyoming news page listed no coal sale after the October 2025 sale; two further news searches found no rescheduled sale, no new bid and no court ruling on the restart. A Wyoming and Montana suit against the 2024 plan amendments (D. Wyo., docket 1:24-cv-00257) is listed on a litigation tracker with an intervention order of 2025-06-06 as the latest event found; its current status was not verified, and no suit against the restart itself was found. The 2026-08-20 Paperwork Reduction Act notice on coal management information collection is not a leasing action.
